mainTopic: How a בית דין questions witnesses and votes in a capital case, and the source in the פסוקים for the seven חקירות.
overview: This amud covers the whole משנה on how a בית דין judges a capital case. It opens with the seven חקירות about when and where the act happened (רבי יוסי says only three are needed). It adds questions about who the person is, whether he was warned, and details of the act. Asking extra detail questions (בדיקות) is praised. Not knowing the answer to a חקירה voids the testimony, but not knowing a בדיקה does not. Witnesses who contradict each other are thrown out, though small, honest gaps in the date or hour are forgiven, and רבי יהודה allows even more room. The judges then deliberate, always leaning toward זכות: they open with acquittal, silence a witness who argues and a student who argues for conviction, delay a conviction overnight, and let judges switch only toward acquittal. One extra vote acquits, but conviction needs a majority of two, so judges are added in pairs up to 71. The גמרא then begins by asking where the seven חקירות come from, and רב יהודה finds them in three פסוקים.

steps.title: The seven core questions about time and place
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that בית דין examines witnesses with seven חקירות covering the cycle of years, the year, the month, the date, the day, the hour and the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: The court would question the witnesses with seven questions: in which seven-year cycle, in which year, in which month, on what date of the month, on which day, at which hour, and in what place.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens by listing the seven basic questions that every witness in a capital case must be asked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All seven questions pin down exactly when and where the act happened. They narrow the time step by step, from the large seven-year cycle down to the exact hour, and then fix the place.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; marks the start of the משנה text
The core questions about time and place
Here, a seven-year cycle (שמיטה cycle), not a week

steps.whyThisMatters: These precise time-and-place questions are what make it possible to test the witnesses, for example by showing they were somewhere else at that time.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
They would examine them (the witnesses)
with seven interrogations:
In which seven-year cycle, in which year,
phrases.notes: שבוע here means a seven-year cycle of years, not a week of days.

phrases.english: in which month, on what date of the month,
on which day (of the week), at which hour,
in what place.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses in capital cases are asked seven questions about time and place.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: only three questions are needed
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי disagrees and holds that only the day, the hour and the place are core questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: on which day, at which hour, in what place.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי offers a different view. He says the core questions are only three, not seven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא counted seven questions, starting from the seven-year cycle. רבי יוסי keeps only the day, the hour and the place, so the bigger time frames are not part of his list of core questions.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֵיזֶה יוֹם, בְּאֵיזוֹ שָׁעָה, בְּאֵיזֶה מָקוֹם.
phrases.english: On which day, at which hour, in what place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A disagreeing opinion about how many core questions are asked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only three core questions are asked: day, hour and place.

steps.title: Do you recognize him, and did you warn him?
steps.stepSummary: The judges also ask the witnesses whether they recognize the accused and whether they gave him a warning (התראה).
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you recognize him? Did you warn him?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds two more questions. The judges check that the witnesses know who the person is and that they warned him before he sinned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These questions are not about time or place. They are about the person himself: is this really the one who did it, and did he receive the required התראה before acting.

keyTerms.meaning: A warning given before the sin

phrases.english: Do you recognize him?
Did you warn him?

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The witnesses are asked if they recognize the accused and if they warned him.

steps.title: Details of the act: the idol worship example
steps.stepSummary: For someone accused of עבודה זרה, the judges ask which idol he worshipped and how he worshipped it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For one who worships idols, they ask: whom did he worship, and how did he worship?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives an example of questions about the act itself, using an accused idol worshipper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the questions move to the details of the sin. For עבודה זרה, the judges ask which idol it was and what form of worship he used.

keyTerms.meaning: With what, or in what way

phrases.english: One who worships idols:
whom did he worship,
and in what way did he worship?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָעוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֶת מִי עָבַד
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses are asked about the specific details of the act, such as which idol was worshipped and how.

steps.title: Adding more detail questions is praiseworthy
steps.stepSummary: A judge who asks more בדיקות (detail questions) deserves praise.
steps.simpleTranslation: Anyone who increases the examinations is praiseworthy.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה praises judges who ask the witnesses many extra detail questions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Beyond the fixed questions, a judge may keep asking about small details. The more he asks, the more likely he is to uncover false testimony, so this is praised.

phrases.english: Anyone who increases the examinations –
this one is praiseworthy.

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּל הַמַּרְבֶּה בִּבְדִיקוֹת הֲרֵי זֶה מְשׁוּבָּח
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Asking many detail questions is praiseworthy.

steps.title: בן זכאי questioned witnesses about fig stems
steps.stepSummary: A story shows the praise in action: בן זכאי examined witnesses even about the stems of figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and בן זכאי examined the witnesses about the stems of figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה backs up the praise of extra questions with a real story about בן זכאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן זכאי asked about a tiny detail, the stems of figs at the scene. This shows how far a judge may go with בדיקות to test the witnesses.

phrases.english: There was an incident, and ben Zakkai examined
about the stems of figs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story that illustrates the rule that extra questions are praiseworthy.
steps.raayaObject: That asking many detail questions is praiseworthy
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of בן זכאי asking about fig stems

steps.title: What is the difference between the two kinds of questions?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how חקירות and בדיקות differ.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between interrogations and examinations?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks a question to set up the next step, which explains how the two kinds of questions differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far both kinds of questions were listed. Now the משנה wants to know what practical difference there is between the core חקירות and the extra בדיקות.

phrases.english: What is the difference between interrogations and examinations?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical legal difference between חקירות and בדיקות

steps.title: Saying "I don't know": void for חקירות, still valid for בדיקות
steps.stepSummary: If even one witness cannot answer a חקירה, the testimony is void. For בדיקות, the testimony stands even if both witnesses cannot answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: For interrogations, if one says "I do not know," their testimony is void. For examinations, if one says "I do not know," and even if two say "We do not know," their testimony stands.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its question. A witness who does not know the answer to a core question ruins the testimony, but not knowing a detail question does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חקירות are required for valid testimony, so one "I don't know" cancels it. The בדיקות are extra, so even when both witnesses don't know the answer, the testimony is still accepted.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two words: חקירות are the core time-and-place questions, where not knowing cancels the testimony. בדיקות are the extra detail questions, where not knowing does not.

phrases.english: Interrogations – if one says "I do not know,"
their testimony is void.
Examinations – if one says "I do not know,"
and even if two say "We do not know,"
their testimony stands.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲקִירוֹת אֶחָד אוֹמֵר אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ עֵדוּתָן בְּטֵילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how חקירות and בדיקות differ.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not knowing a חקירה voids the testimony; not knowing a בדיקה does not, even if both witnesses don't know.

steps.title: Contradiction voids testimony in both kinds of questions
steps.stepSummary: Whether in חקירות or בדיקות, if the witnesses contradict each other, their testimony is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both with interrogations and with examinations, when they contradict each other, their testimony is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with the rule the two kinds of questions share: if the witnesses give clashing answers, the testimony is thrown out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not knowing a detail is forgivable, but giving opposite answers is not. A contradiction, even on a small בדיקה, shows the two witnesses are not telling one consistent story.
steps.whatToRemember: There are seven core חקירות (רבי יוסי: three) plus extra בדיקות. Not knowing a חקירה voids testimony; not knowing a בדיקה does not. Contradicting each other on either kind voids the testimony.

phrases.english: Both interrogations and examinations,
at a time when they contradict one another –
their testimony is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד חֲקִירוֹת וְאֶחָד בְּדִיקוֹת בִּזְמַן שֶׁמַּכְחִישִׁין זֶה אֶת זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the shared rule after the difference was explained.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Contradiction between the witnesses voids the testimony, whether it happens in a חקירה or a בדיקה.

steps.title: A one-day difference in the date does not cancel the testimony
steps.stepSummary: If one witness says the 2nd of the month and the other says the 3rd, the testimony stands. One of them may simply not know that the previous month had an extra day.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says, 'It happened on the 2nd of the month,' and the other says, 'On the 3rd of the month.' Their testimony stands. This is because one of them knows the month was made longer by a day, and the other does not know it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a first limit to the rule from step 9. Not every difference counts as a contradiction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said contradicting witnesses are void. Here the משנה explains that a one-day gap in the date is not a real contradiction. It can come from honest confusion about whether the last month had 29 or 30 days. Both witnesses may be describing the same actual day.

keyTerms.meaning: The adding of an extra day to a month (making it 30 days instead of 29)
One witness says, and the other witness says

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the witnesses are describing two different days. The משנה's point is that they may both mean the same real day and only count it differently.

phrases.english: One witness says: 'On the second of the month,'
and one witness says: 'On the third of the month' —
their testimony stands,
because this one knows that a day was added to the month,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ בְּעִיבּוּרוֹ שֶׁל חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: and that one does not know that a day was added to the month.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בִּשְׁנַיִם בְּחֹדֶשׁ״, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה בַּחֹדֶשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the rule of step 9: a small, explainable date gap is not a contradiction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-day difference in the date is excused, and the testimony stands, because it can come from not knowing about עיבור החודש.

steps.title: A two-day difference in the date does cancel the testimony
steps.stepSummary: If one witness says the 3rd and the other says the 5th, the testimony is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says, 'On the 3rd,' and the other says, 'On the 5th.' Their testimony is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה shows where the excuse from step 10 ends. A two-day gap cannot be explained away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Confusion about an added day can only shift the count by one day. A two-day gap cannot come from that confusion, so it counts as a real contradiction. The rule of step 9 applies.

keyTerms.meaning: On the fifth (day of the month)

phrases.english: One says: 'On the third,' and one says: 'On the fifth' —
their testimony is void.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the outer limit of the excuse given in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A two-day difference in the date is a real contradiction, and the testimony is void.

steps.title: Differences in the hour: one hour is excused, two hours are not
steps.stepSummary: The same kind of rule applies to the time of day. A one-hour gap still stands, but a gap from the third to the fifth hour is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: One witness says, 'At the second hour,' and the other says, 'At the third hour.' Their testimony stands. One says, 'At the third,' and the other says, 'At the fifth.' Their testimony is void.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the date to the hour of the day. It draws the same kind of line: a small gap is allowed, but a big gap is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People easily misjudge the hour by about one hour, so a one-hour gap is treated as an honest mistake. A two-hour gap is too big to be a simple guessing error, according to the first opinion (the תנא קמא). This is the view that רבי יהודה will argue with next.

keyTerms.meaning: At the second hour of the day
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

phrases.english: One says: 'At two hours,'
phrases.notes: He means the second hour of the day, counting from sunrise.

phrases.english: and one says: 'At three hours' —
their testimony stands.
One says: 'At three,' and one says: 'At five' —
their testimony is void.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בִּשְׁתֵּי שָׁעוֹת״, וְאֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״בְּשָׁלֹשׁ שָׁעוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the same pattern as steps 10 and 11, but for the hour instead of the date.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A one-hour gap is excused. A two-hour gap (third versus fifth hour) voids the testimony, according to the תנא קמא.

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows a two-hour gap, but not one that crosses noon
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says the third-versus-fifth case still stands. He agrees that fifth versus seventh is void, because by then the sun has moved from east to west.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: it stands. But if one says, 'At the fifth hour,' and the other says, 'At the seventh,' their testimony is void. At the fifth hour the sun is in the east, and at the seventh hour the sun is in the west.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the last ruling of step 12. He then gives his own limit and his reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, a two-hour mistake is still a normal mistake. Once one time is before noon and the other is after noon, though, nobody could honestly confuse them. The sun's side of the sky has changed, so the gap is now a true contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the first opinion here

steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses only contradict each other when the gap is too big to be an honest mistake. A one-day date gap is fine, and so is a one-hour time gap. רבי יהודה even allows two hours, as long as both times are on the same side of noon.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that "contradiction" in עדות is measured by realistic human error, not by exact numbers.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: It stands.
phrases.notes: He is talking about the case just before: one says the third hour, the other says the fifth.

phrases.english: If one says 'At five,' and one says 'At seven' —
their testimony is void,
because at five the sun is in the east
and at seven the sun is in the west.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling at the end of step 12 and gives a wider allowance with its own limit.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A two-hour gap is still valid, but a gap that crosses noon (fifth versus seventh hour) is void, because the sun has moved from east to west.

steps.title: Second witness is checked, then the court opens with acquittal
steps.stepSummary: After the first witness, the second witness is brought in and examined. If their stories match, the court begins deliberating by first seeking reasons to acquit.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then they bring in the second witness and examine him. If their words match, the court opens with זכות.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה picks up its trial procedure. It moves from checking the witnesses to the judges starting to discuss the case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps explained when contradictions cancel the testimony. Here the testimonies are found to match, so the trial can go on. The first thing the judges do is look for ways to acquit, not convict.

keyTerms.meaning: matching, in line with each other
they open with arguments to acquit

steps.whyThisMatters: Opening with זכות sets the tone for the whole capital trial: the court's first instinct is to save a life.

phrases.english: And afterward they bring in the second
and examine him.
If their words are found to match,
they open with acquittal.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַכְנִיסִין אֶת הַשֵּׁנִי וּבוֹדְקִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the trial order after the side rules about dates and hours. The witnesses' words now match.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the two testimonies match, deliberation begins with arguments for acquittal.

steps.title: A witness arguing for acquittal or a student arguing for conviction is silenced
steps.stepSummary: If a witness wants to argue for the accused, or a student wants to argue against him, the court silences him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the עדים says, 'I have a reason to acquit him,' or one of the תלמידים says, 'I have a reason to convict him,' they silence him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists two people who are not allowed to speak in the deliberation: a witness who wants to defend, and a student who wants to accuse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness's job is only to testify, not to argue the case, so even a pro-acquittal argument from him is not heard. Students sitting before the court may help only on the side of זכות. An argument for חובה from them is shut down.

keyTerms.meaning: students who sit before the judges

steps.confusionAlert: The witness is silenced even though he wants to help the accused. The rule is about his role, not about which side he is on.

phrases.english: If one of the witnesses said:
"I have a reason to teach for his acquittal,"
or one of the students said:
"I have a reason to teach for his liability" –
they silence him.
phrases.notes: This covers both people: the witness and the student.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶחָד מִן הָעֵדִים: יֵשׁ לִי לְלַמֵּד עָלָיו זְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Now that the deliberation has opened, the משנה sets limits on who may speak.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A witness may not argue at all, and a student may not argue for conviction.

steps.title: A student arguing for acquittal is seated among the judges
steps.stepSummary: A student who has a reason to acquit is brought up to sit with the judges and stays there the whole day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one of the students says, 'I have a reason to acquit him,' they raise him up, seat him among them, and he does not come down from there all day.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the opposite case: a student who wants to defend the accused is welcomed and joins the judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This contrasts with the previous step. A student's argument for חובה is silenced, but his argument for זכות earns him a seat among the judges. He stays all day so he can keep taking part.

keyTerms.meaning: they raise him up (to the judges' seats)

phrases.english: If one of the students said:
"I have a reason to teach for his acquittal" –
they raise him up and seat him among them,
and he would not come down from there
the whole entire day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אֶחָד מִן הַתַּלְמִידִים: יֵשׁ לִי לְלַמֵּד עָלָיו זְכוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The flip side of step 15: a student arguing for זכות is welcomed, not silenced.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A student with a reason to acquit is seated among the judges for the rest of the day.

steps.title: Real arguments are heard, even from the accused himself
steps.stepSummary: The student's argument is accepted only if it has substance. Even the accused may offer a reason to acquit himself, if it has substance.
steps.simpleTranslation: If his words have substance, they listen to him. Even if the accused himself says, 'I have a reason to acquit myself,' they listen to him, as long as his words have substance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a condition to the student's argument and extends the right to argue for זכות even to the accused.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being seated is not enough. The argument must actually hold up. The accused, who obviously has a personal stake, is still heard, but only if his point is real.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ בִּדְבָרָיו, שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ.
phrases.english: If there is substance in his words, they listen to him.
And even if he says:
"I have a reason to teach for my own acquittal,"
they listen to him,
as long as there is substance in his words.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם יֵשׁ מַמָּשׁ בִּדְבָרָיו, שׁוֹמְעִין לוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a condition to the student's argument and widens the circle to the accused.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any argument for acquittal, even from the accused, is heard if it has real substance.

steps.title: If not acquitted, the verdict waits for the next day
steps.stepSummary: If the court finds to acquit, he is freed. If not, the case is pushed to the next day. The judges discuss in pairs, eat little, drink no wine, deliberate all night, and return early.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they found זכות for him, they free him. If not, they push it off to tomorrow and pair up. They would eat less, drink no wine all day, discuss all night, and the next morning come early to the בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what happens after the first day's discussion: immediate release, or a delay with serious overnight deliberation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A guilty verdict is not given on the same day. The delay gives one more chance to find זכות. Eating less and avoiding wine keep the judges clear-headed for that night of discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: they put his case off to the next day

steps.confusionAlert: "If not" does not mean he was convicted. It means there was not yet a decision to acquit, so they wait before ruling.

phrases.english: And if they found a reason to acquit him, they released him.
And if not, they put him off to tomorrow,
and they pair up, pairs by pairs.
They would eat less food,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא הָיוּ שׁוֹתִין יַיִן כׇּל הַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: and they would not drink wine all day,
and they discuss back and forth all night.
And the next day they rise early and come to court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the arguments are heard, the משנה gives the outcome of the first day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Without acquittal, the verdict is delayed overnight while the judges deliberate soberly in pairs.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a conviction in דיני נפשות can never be rushed into on the same day.

steps.title: Next day: judges restate their views, and may only switch toward acquittal
steps.stepSummary: Each judge restates yesterday's position. A judge who argued for conviction may switch to acquittal, but one who argued for acquittal may not switch to conviction.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who acquits says, 'I acquitted, and I stand by my acquittal.' The one who convicts says, 'I convicted, and I stand by it.' One who taught חובה may now teach זכות, but one who taught זכות cannot go back and teach חובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes the second morning: judges declare where they stand, and it sets a one-way rule about changing your mind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing one's mind is allowed only in the direction of saving the accused. A judge who argued to acquit is locked into that side, so arguments for חובה can only shrink, never grow.

keyTerms.meaning: in my place, I stand where I was

steps.confusionAlert: The judge who convicted is not required to keep convicting. He just states his view, and he is free to move to זכות.

phrases.english: The one who acquits says:
"I acquit, and I acquit in my place."
phrases.notes: He means: I said acquit yesterday, and I still stand by it.

phrases.english: And the one who convicts says:
"I convict, and I convict in my place."
One who taught for liability may teach for acquittal,
but one who taught for acquittal
cannot go back and teach for liability.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְזַכֶּה אוֹמֵר: אֲנִי מְזַכֶּה, וּמְזַכֶּה אֲנִי בִּמְקוֹמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next morning that step 18 set up.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judges may retract only from חובה to זכות, never from זכות to חובה.

steps.title: Scribes correct mistakes, then the judges count the vote
steps.stepSummary: If a judge mixes up what he said, the judges' scribes remind him. If acquittal is found, he is freed. Otherwise they stand and count; twelve to acquit against eleven to convict means acquittal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they made a mistake, the two scribes of the judges remind him. If they found זכות, they free him; if not, they stand for a count. Twelve acquitting and eleven convicting: he is acquitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה handles memory mistakes and then moves to the formal vote, giving the first counting result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The scribes' written record keeps a judge from wrongly switching sides, which matters because of the one-way rule in step 19. When there is no clear acquittal, they vote. A majority of just one is enough to acquit.

keyTerms.meaning: the judges' scribes who record what each judge said
they stand to count the votes

steps.whatToRemember: Throughout this משנה every rule leans toward זכות: open with acquittal, silence arguments for conviction from students, delay any conviction, allow switching only to acquittal, and acquit by a majority of one.

phrases.english: If they erred in the matter –
the two scribes of the judges remind him.
If they found a reason to acquit him – they released him,
and if not – they stand for the count.
Twelve acquit
and eleven convict – he is acquitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: טָעוּ בַּדָּבָר – שְׁנֵי סוֹפְרֵי הַדַּיָּינִין מַזְכִּירִין אוֹתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Protects the one-way rule of step 19 with the scribes' record, then moves to the final vote.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scribes correct a judge's memory; if there is no clear acquittal they count votes, and a 12 to 11 majority acquits.

steps.title: When the court of 23 cannot decide, add judges
steps.stepSummary: Three deadlock cases: 12 to 11 for conviction, 11 to 11 with one unsure, and 22 with one unsure. In each case more judges are added.
steps.simpleTranslation: If twelve judges say 'guilty' and eleven say 'innocent', or eleven say 'innocent', eleven say 'guilty' and one says 'I don't know', or even twenty-two vote either way and one says 'I don't know', then more judges are added to the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists the situations where the 23 judges have no valid verdict, and rules that the court must grow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A capital conviction needs a majority of at least two, so 12 to 11 for 'guilty' is not enough. A judge who says 'I don't know' counts as if he were not there. That leaves only 22 voting judges, which is not a full court of 23, so more judges must be added.

keyTerms.meaning: Judges who vote to find him liable (guilty)
'I do not know'. This judge has no opinion and is treated as not voting.
They add more judges to the court

steps.confusionAlert: Twelve against eleven sounds like a majority, but it is not enough to convict in a capital case. For a death sentence the majority must be at least two votes.

phrases.english: If twelve find him liable
and eleven acquit,
or even if eleven acquit
and eleven find him liable
and one says, "I do not know,"

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲפִילּוּ עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁנַיִם מְזַכִּין אוֹ מְחַיְּיבִין
phrases.english: or even if twenty-two acquit or find him liable
and one says, "I do not know"
they add more judges.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the counting from step 20. That step showed when the count acquits; this one shows when no valid verdict comes out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When no valid verdict is reached (conviction by only one vote, or a judge says 'I do not know'), judges are added.

steps.title: Adding judges two at a time, up to 71
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how many judges are added and answers: two at a time, up to a maximum of 71.
steps.simpleTranslation: How many do they add? Two at a time, until there are seventy-one.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks itself a quick question and answers it, explaining how the court grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Adding two at a time keeps the number of judges odd (25, 27, and so on), so an even tie can be avoided. The limit is 71, the size of the great סנהדרין, and no more judges are added after that.

keyTerms.meaning: And how many do they add?
Seventy-one, the maximum size of the court

phrases.english: And how many do they add?
Two at a time,
up to seventy-one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the details of the rule in step 21 ('add judges').
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Judges are added in pairs, up to a maximum of 71.

steps.title: The final vote of 71: acquit by one, but never convict by one
steps.stepSummary: With 71 judges, 36 to 35 for acquittal frees him. 36 to 35 for conviction means they keep debating until a judge who wants to convict switches to acquittal.
steps.simpleTranslation: If thirty-six acquit and thirty-five convict, he is innocent. If thirty-six convict and thirty-five acquit, the two sides argue with each other until one of the convicting judges comes to agree with those who acquit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the end of the process, once the court has reached its full 71 judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Acquittal works with a one-vote majority, but conviction does not, even at 71. Since no more judges can be added, the only way forward is more debate. The משנה describes the hoped-for outcome: one convicting judge is persuaded by the acquitting side.

keyTerms.meaning: They debate, one side against the other
Until he 'sees', meaning he becomes convinced

steps.whatToRemember: In a capital case, acquittal needs only a one-vote majority, but conviction needs at least two. Judges are added in pairs up to 71, and after that the court only debates.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how strongly the court leans toward saving a life. Even the largest court never sentences someone to death by a single vote.

phrases.english: If thirty-six acquit
and thirty-five find him liable, he is acquitted.
If thirty-six find him liable
and thirty-five acquit,
they debate, these against those,
until one of those finding him liable sees
the words of those who acquit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the process from steps 21-22 by showing what happens once the court reaches 71.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At 71, a one-vote majority acquits, but a one-vote majority to convict leads only to more debate.

steps.title: Where do the seven questions come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source of the seven questions (שבע חקירות) that the witnesses are asked.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Where do we learn these things from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its discussion and asks for the source of a rule in the משנה. This sets up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question does not go back to the voting rules just learned. It goes back to the start of this משנה, which listed seven questions the court asks witnesses about the time and place of the crime. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind that list.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
'From where are these things learned?' This asks for a source.
The seven questions put to witnesses about the time and place of the crime

steps.confusionAlert: 'These things' does not mean the 36-35 vote that came right before. It means the seven questions to the witnesses from the beginning of this משנה.

phrases.english: GEMARA: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: The גמרא is asking about the seven questions the witnesses are asked, from the start of this משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the end of the משנה to the start of the גמרא, and goes back to the opening rule of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the פסוקים for the seven questions put to witnesses.

steps.title: רב יהודה finds the seven questions in three פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes three פסוקים whose words for 'inquire', 'investigate' and 'diligently' together add up to seven questions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: as the פסוק says, 'You shall inquire, investigate, and ask diligently,' and it says, 'It is told to you, and you hear, and inquire diligently,' and it says, 'The judges shall inquire diligently.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by bringing three פסוקים about court investigations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word of investigating counts as one required question. 'Inquire' (ודרשת / ודרשו) appears three times, 'investigate' (וחקרת) once, and 'diligently' (היטב) three times. Together that makes seven questions.

keyTerms.meaning: 'As the פסוק says.' This brings a source from the תורה.

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the careful questioning of witnesses is not just good practice. The תורה requires it, through the repeated words for investigating.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
As the verse states:
"And you shall inquire, and investigate, and ask diligently,"
and it says: "And it is told to you, and you hear, and inquire diligently,"
and it says: "And the judges shall inquire diligently."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The seven questions come from counting the investigation words in דברים 13:15, 17:4 and 19:18.
